newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds steadily slid down on Thursday, but recovered some of their losses at the close as U.S. Treasuries improved, dealers said.

Today's batch of data from the United States was largely in line with expectations and the mild 0.1 percent rise in consumer prices in April, for example, helped lift Treasuries out of their early trough.
"The CPI's were in line. The rest of the figures were largely bond-friendly," one Dutch trader said.

However, nerves persisted in the Dutch market ahead of the next FOMC meeting on May 20 and a possible hike in U.S. interest rates. Traders said the two-month highs bonds reached recently were unlikely to be revisited.
"It's a cautious attitude we have at the moment," one dealer said.
Dutch bonds themselves came under some added pressure at the long end after the early issuance of a 1.25 billion guilder 15-year bond from Italy.
Traders said they had noticed the April 2010 paper being sold from Wednesday.
"Clearly there was some hedging going on with, say, the 2010s. There's a bit of pressure there today too," one trader said.
Some traders added that a possible reopening of the Dutch February 2007 bonds next week was placing some additional pressure at the ten year part of the curve.
At the shorter end, demand showed some signs of improvement and the spread over bunds narrowed.
"The short end is well bid. There is some concern (in the Netherlands) about money growth, but it looks like a reasonable buy," one trader said.
